newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Goldsmith's Europe of Nations to reform.
newsitem.headline: Goldsmith's Europe of Nations to reform.

text.p: The defunct Europe of Nations (EDN) group in the European Parliament, led by British billionaire James Goldsmith, is expected to announce its revival on December 10, an EDN official said on Thursday.
"The members will announce (the decision) at a press conference in Strasbourg next Tuesday," the official told Reuters.
He declined to confirm the names of the Euro-MPs expected to join the former members of the anti-federalist EDN and reconstitute the group.
"We will know tomorrow. There will be one (new) member, perhaps two," another EDN official said.
Parliament sources said the most likely candidate was Hans Kronberger, a Euro-MP elected on October 13 from the list put up by Joerg Haidar's far-right Austrian Freedom Party (FPO).
They cited two other FPO members, Peter Sichrovsky and Klaus Lukas, and British Conservative James Nicholson as possible new EDN members.
The EDN collapsed in November following the defection to the Christian Democrat European People's Party (EPP) of Anne Christine Poisson, one of its French members.
Poisson's departure left the EDN with 17 members -- one short of the minimum needed to form a group.
After weeks of rumours in and around parliament that the EDN was wooing Haidar's FPO to stave off collapse, the EDN in October issued a statement denying all contacts with "extremists".

When the party officially collpased in November, the former EDN Euro-MPs found themselves relegated to the non-aligned benches, alongside the members from the FPO and the French National Front of Jean-Marie Le Pen.
Kronberger, Sichrovsky and Lukas were elected on the platform put up by the FPO but were not actually members of the Freedom Party, one parliament source said.
